newsitem.title: CHINA: China to raise electricity charges from May 1.
newsitem.headline: China to raise electricity charges from May 1.

text.p: China will raise electricity prices from May 1, an official of the State Planning Commission said on Tuesday.
He declined to give the size of the increase, saying it would differ from region to region depending on the local grid.
The fee for private households in Beijing would increase to 0.3618 yuan per kilowatt hour from the current 0.313, the Beijing Daily said.
The planning commission official attributed the increase to the rising price of coal and to higher generating costs.
The price increase follows widespread speculation about price rises following the recent creation of the China National Electricity Corp, which will eventually replace the Ministry of Power Industry.
The formation of the company has been widely seen as a way to make the power sector operate more on market principles.
Electricity price adjustments in China are under strict state control.
Minister of Power Shi Dazhen said last week that while electricity prices had doubled in the past two decades, the increase was far less than the rise in the overall price index.
